subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk delegates orchestration to Presentation. The shared Scene renders through SceneLayer and scene-kit nodes, while Stage supplies the active step payload. The demo does not implement a parallel stage or navigation mechanism.
evidence: Talk passes STEPS to Presentation; Scene renders SceneLayer with Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, and SymbolChip nodes.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: STEPS creates all nine steps with the same Scene and groupKey. Stage derives a stable group scene key and retains that scene across adjacent grouped steps. Separately, presentation-owned ENTITY values pass as node IDs, and the node components assign those IDs to Motion layoutId.
evidence: STEPS maps every title to Scene with groupKey 'how-to-story'; the focused test asserts this for every step.
Scene passes ENTITY values to Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, and Frame; each consumer sets layoutId={id}.

criteria.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons expose semantic current state and stable data-active hooks. The demo's local CSS targets those hooks. Footer implements the default attribution link in project source, and the focused test checks its label and target.

criteria.rationale: The registry only maps the demo slug to Talk. subcomponents.title: Preview addressing and runtime/step error detection

criteria.rationale: The shared preview launcher binds, probes, and constructs its browser URL using 127.0.0.1.
evidence: `findFreePort()` listens on `host`, `startPreview()` passes `host` to Vite and fetches its URL, and both verifier and inspector navigate using that returned URL.

criteria.rationale: Readiness checks whether the child has exited, but a successful HTTP response is not tied to that child. A stale responder could answer during the port handoff before the child’s exit is observed; the verifier also does not monitor child exit after readiness.
evidence: `waitForPreview()` accepts `fetch(url)` when `response.ok` and the child has not yet reported exit; `verify.mjs` proceeds without further child-status checks.

criteria.rationale: The verifier collects console and page errors, but the focused runtime test only asserts an injected error message at step 3. It does not assert propagation of a console error and a page error separately.
evidence: The `runtime-fault` test injects a render exception and matches `injected runtime fault`; no focused test injects and asserts a console error diagnostic.

criteria.rationale: A focused test stalls navigation and asserts a nonzero verification failure naming the target step.
evidence: The `transition-fault` test changes `next` navigation to retain the index and expects `Render check failed at step 2: transition did not advance`; `expectFailure()` checks nonzero status.

subcomponents.title: Complete, settled screenshot capture

criteria.rationale: The project provides a separate local inspection command that launches a browser and writes screenshots.
evidence: The `inspect` package script invokes `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs`; `inspect()` calls `page.screenshot()` for each step, and the skill directs users to invoke the command.

criteria.rationale: The helper visits the requested route on its preview, checks each step index, and saves a screenshot for each index. A two-step integration fixture asserts both screenshot files are produced.
evidence: `inspect()` loops over `stepCount`, checks `data-step-index`, advances with ArrowRight, and screenshots each step; the inspection fixture expects both `inspection-fixture-01.png` and `inspection-fixt…

criteria.rationale: Capture waits a fixed interval without observing animation completion or using a transition contract consumed by the persistent scene motion. The test’s 400 ms animation and 500 ms wait establish only that fixture’s timing.
evidence: `inspect()` calls `delay(settleMs)` before capture; `Stage` uses motion transitions independently, and the integration test overrides the delay rather than testing a completion condition.

subcomponents.title: Overlap, active-state, and attribution warnings

criteria.rationale: The test asserts that allowed text is absent from warnings, but its two allowed spans are in normal inline flow and are not made to overlap. That assertion cannot prove the marker suppresses an intentional collision while preserving unrelated warnings.
evidence: The fixture places two spans inside `.allowed` without collision styling; `expect(output).not.toMatch(/Allowed overlap/)` would pass even if marker suppression were removed.

criteria.rationale: The helper compares rendered active and inactive control styles, and a focused fixture makes those styles equal and asserts the warning.
evidence: `findChromeWarnings()` compares computed color, background, opacity, border, weight, decoration, and width; the inspection test applies identical control styles and matches the indistinct-state warni…

criteria.rationale: The helper detects browser-default link color, and the inspection fixture asserts that warning for the default attribution link.
evidence: `findChromeWarnings()` checks the attribution link’s computed color against browser-default colors; the test expects `browser-default link styling` in inspector output.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk delegates orchestration to Presentation. The shared Scene renders through SceneLayer and scene-kit nodes, while Stage supplies the active step payload. The demo does not implement a parallel stage or navigation mechanism.
evidence: Talk passes STEPS to Presentation; Scene renders SceneLayer with Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, and SymbolChip nodes.

demo-integration.rationale: STEPS creates all nine steps with the same Scene and groupKey. Stage derives a stable group scene key and retains that scene across adjacent grouped steps. Separately, presentation-owned ENTITY values pass as node IDs, and the node components assign those IDs to Motion layoutId.
evidence: STEPS maps every title to Scene with groupKey 'how-to-story'; the focused test asserts this for every step.
Scene passes ENTITY values to Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, and Frame; each consumer sets layoutId={id}.

demo-integration.rationale: The delivered Talk supplies the required title, and Presentation passes it to Header and Footer, where it is rendered. Presentation also uses the shared design defaults, and Stage uses the shared timing constants. The inspected public inputs and shared constants on this path have concrete consumers.
evidence: Talk's title reaches Header's browse heading and Footer's screen-reader title.
Presentation resolves dimensions from DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H; Stage consumes LAYOUT_T, ENTER_T, and ENTER_DELAY.

demo-integration.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons expose semantic current state and stable data-active hooks. The demo's local CSS targets those hooks. Footer implements the default attribution link in project source, and the focused test checks its label and target.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc buttons set aria-current and data-active from the active index.
Footer supplies the default attribution link; Presentation.test.tsx asserts its rendered label and href.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry only maps the demo slug to Talk. Talk supplies local steps and styling to the shared Presentation boundary; the scene data, entity IDs, and demo styles stay in the presentation directory. Presentation contains reusable orchestration rather than demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry loads Talk; Talk imports local STEPS and style.css and calls Presentation.
The complete presentation-local implementation is Talk, steps, entities, and CSS; Presentation handles generic steps, chrome, Stage, and navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: Each step requires a stable id and narration fields, and Presentation selects the active step for its scene and chrome.
evidence: StepMeta requires id, era, title, and caption; Presentation passes the selected step to Stage, Header, and Footer.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed numbers come from the active array index.
evidence: Header renders index + 1; Footer labels progress buttons from their array positions.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic Step binds its payload type to its Scene component, and Stage passes that payload into the scene.
evidence: Step<TPayload> declares payload and ComponentType<SceneProps<TPayload>>; Stage renders Scene with step.payload.

scene-kit.rationale: Persistent entities have stable layout IDs within a retained grouped scene, enabling layout animation across updates.
evidence: Box and other entity primitives set layout and layoutId from id; Stage retains the group key and LayoutGroup across adjacent grouped steps.

scene-kit.rationale: Newcomer entry waits on a fixed delay that the continuing entity motion does not consume; there is no completion signal linking them.
evidence: Appear uses ENTER_DELAY, while Box's layout animation has no transition using that value. Stage's LAYOUT_T applies to the scene wrapper, and its separate timing div does not control newcomer …

scene-kit.rationale: The scene boundary retains exiting whole scenes, but ordinary entities removed conditionally inside a retained grouped scene have no general exit mechanism.
evidence: Stage's AnimatePresence wraps the scene div, not its conditional child entities. The sample Scene conditionally renders ordinary Box and other nodes; those primitives provide no removal-preservin…

scene-kit.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key and Scene reuse the keyed scene and receive updated payloads.
evidence: Stage derives one group key and renders the same Scene with the active payload; the grouped-scene test asserts that the scene DOM instance is unchanged after navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene remains mounted, so continuing child instances retain their state and avoid a new initial animation.
evidence: Stage uses the same scene key and Scene component for grouped updates; its grouped branch has no initial entry state. The sample uses stable entity IDs across its group.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample implements one evolving grouped diagram with positioned, persistent entities and additions driven by step payload.
evidence: All sample steps use one Scene and groupKey; Scene reads payload.through, retains earlier entities, and adds positioned cards, connections, and a final frame.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode renders the active scene and title while omitting browse-only reading controls and table of contents.
evidence: Presentation gates Toc to browse mode; Footer's present branch renders step.title instead of the caption, progress, and previous/next controls.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode provides the active title and caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer renders these active-step elements in its browse branch; Presentation renders Toc in browse mode, and the sample CSS lays it out as a horizontal table of contents on wide viewports.

scene-kit.rationale: Toggling mode changes only mode state, leaving the selected index intact.
evidence: usePresentationNav stores index and mode separately; its toggleMode updates mode only. The focused test switches modes at step index 1 and asserts that index remains 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The navigation hook maps supported presentation keys to next, previous, and mode toggle actions.
evidence: onKeyDown handles ArrowRight, PageDown, Space, ArrowLeft, PageUp, and P, and installs a window keydown listener.

scene-kit.rationale: The swipe handler rejects predominantly vertical motion but does not track or reject multi-touch gestures, and no focused assertions cover both rejection cases.
evidence: The touch handlers record X and Y from changedTouches[0] and compare distances, but never inspect touch count; the focused Presentation tests contain no vertical or multi-touch swipe assertions.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents controls call a bounded direct-jump action.
evidence: Footer progress buttons call goTo(item), Toc buttons call goTo(target), and the focused test clicks Go to step 2 and asserts index 1.

scene-kit.rationale: Current progress and table-of-contents items expose semantic current state and stable active hooks.
evidence: Footer and Toc set aria-current and data-active from the active index; the focused test asserts those attributes on initial render.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation keyboard navigation returns early when focus is on an interactive control, preserving that control's keyboard behavior.
evidence: isInteractive checks buttons, links, form fields, and other controls; the focused test sends ArrowRight to a focused progress button and asserts the step does not change.

scene-kit.rationale: Previous navigation cannot select an index below zero.
evidence: prev clamps with Math.max(0, index - 1); the focused test clicks Previous on the first step and asserts index 0.

scene-kit.rationale: Next and direct navigation cannot select an index past the final step.
evidence: next and goTo clamp against count - 1; the focused test clicks Next at the last step and asserts index 1 remains selected.

scene-kit.rationale: The stage uses one scale factor, but its fit calculation can exceed the area the stage actually occupies at an ordinary viewport.
evidence: useFitScale computes present-mode height from window.innerHeight minus 74 and 76, while sample CSS constrains the stage with 78px top and 150px bottom in both modes. At 1024×600, the fit remains 1 fo…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Presentation passes those defaults to Stage, which applies them to the canvas dimensions.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit exposes stable class and data hooks for presentation-owned styling.
evidence: Presentation, Stage, Footer, and Box render stable presentation, stage, attribution, and entity hooks; the sample stylesheet targets those hooks.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit primitives supply structural positioning and animation without a built-in visual theme; the sample owns the visual declarations.
evidence: SceneLayer supplies absolute positioning, Box forwards authored style and className, and sample CSS defines colors, type, borders, and card treatments. The focused test checks node sources for visual…

scene-kit.rationale: The kit and bootstrap use plain CSS and do not require a styling framework.
evidence: The bootstrap dependency list contains React, Motion, and tooling without a CSS framework; its stylesheet is plain CSS, and the sample imports presentation-owned CSS.

scene-kit.rationale: SceneLayer and entity style props support explicit coordinates for diagrams.
evidence: SceneLayer establishes an absolute layer, Box forwards CSSProperties, and the sample Scene gives persistent entities explicit left, top, width, height, and inset values.

scene-kit.rationale: The default link exists, but the kit does not place it at the bottom-right corner; that placement comes from sample-owned CSS.
evidence: Footer renders the default link in presentation-attribution. Kit layout CSS positions the footer but gives attribution no corner position; the sample stylesheet supplies position:absolute, right, and…

scene-kit.rationale: The default attribution has a stable hook targetable by host styling.
evidence: Footer wraps attribution in presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution; the sample stylesheet targets that class.

scene-kit.rationale: The header renders no default brand, and callers can explicitly supply one.
evidence: Header renders only the optional brand prop in its brand slot; Presentation passes its optional brand prop through. The focused test asserts no header link on default render.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires asking for missing topic, style, and step details one question at a time, waiting for each answer before asking the next.
evidence: The new-presentation interview lists the details in order and explicitly requires the next missing question only after the previous answer.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly permits the user to proceed with partial details and requires building from the information captured.
evidence: The interview offers a partial-detail choice, rejects a completeness gate, and directs the agent to label its own design decisions.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs the agent to use supplied details and proceed without questions when the prompt already provides topic, style, and steps.
evidence: The request-handling section explicitly bypasses redundant questions for a complete prompt.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused test copies the bootstrap into a fresh temporary app, installs its dependencies there, and verifies that it builds and renders.
evidence: The bootstrap integration test creates a temporary target, copies the bootstrap, runs npm ci with that target as cwd, then runs build, verify, and inspect with assertions on the screenshot output.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy says to reuse an app with all anchors, but no focused test or verified workflow record constructs an already scaffolded target and checks that its files and presentations are preserved.
evidence: The bootstrap integration test constructs only a fresh target and copies the full bootstrap into it.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused executable evidence constructs a target with only some anchors and verifies that only missing infrastructure is added while existing anchors survive.
evidence: The bootstrap integration test starts from a fresh target and performs a full template copy; it does not set up a partial scaffold.

presentation-skill.rationale: The materialized bootstrap test checks the dependency contract, rejects Tailwind, and builds and renders the copied app. Inspection of every bootstrap scene-kit source closes the test’s narrower style check: the kit supplies motion, layout geometry, navigation, markup hooks, and caller-provided style hooks, with no palette, font, border, shadow, card, button, or theme defaults. The host CSS is a structural reset, and the starter presentation adds no visual styles.
evidence: The bootstrap test copies the template into a temporary app, checks that its manifest has no Tailwind dependency, compares every production kit file with the canonical kit, checks kit node sources fo…

The full bootstrap kit source contains no visual theme declarations; its inline styles set canvas dimensions and scaling or layer positioning, while node style props pass through author-supplied styl…
The bootstrap host CSS sets box sizing, minimum dimensions, margin, and inherited control fonts. The starter stylesheet has no declarations, and the starter scene supplies no visual styles.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap test resolves its template from the test file's source location rather than the shell cwd, copies it to a resolved temporary target, and installs dependencies with that target as cwd.
evidence: The test derives repository from import.meta.url, forms the bootstrap path from it, copies to app, and calls npm ci through run(..., app). The skill directs template lookup relative to SKILL.md.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy specifies a presentations/ target for monorepos, but no focused evidence creates a workspace or apps/packages layout and verifies that target and its dependencies.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates a fresh temporary app without a monorepo declaration or layout.

presentation-skill.rationale: The empty-directory bootstrap test does not exercise the separate standalone-project branch with an existing standalone project and verify scaffolding at that project's root.
evidence: The test's materialized-app target starts as a fresh temporary path; no standalone project state is constructed before copying.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires confirmation before writing to a nonempty project missing anchors, but no focused test or verified workflow record supplies that target state, a user choice, and resulting mutations.
evidence: The only bootstrap target in the integration test is fresh; the test has no confirmation branch or nonempty-target fixture.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a separate presentation folder and registry entry, and the implemented registry and app router load a presentation by its slug.
evidence: The skill directs adding one registry entry. The registry maps the example slug to a lazy Talk import, and App selects the registered component from the URL path.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy assigns visual styling to presentation CSS, and the delivered presentation imports its own stylesheet while the kit accepts class names and styles without supplying a fixed theme.
evidence: Talk imports local style.css; that file defines the presentation's colors, typography, and control treatments. Presentation forwards className and style onto its root.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly forbids overwriting or restructuring other registered presentations, and the registry uses independent entries and lazy imports that support adding another presentation.
evidence: The create and modify instructions require preserving other presentations and routes. The registry's entry structure and route map select each presentation by slug.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires identifying a unique presentation before modifying it and asking the user to choose from registered presentations when the target is ambiguous.
evidence: The modification instructions explicitly place target selection before editing and direct the agent to list registered presentations when needed.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly confines modifications to the selected presentation and host or registry files strictly needed for the request.
evidence: The modification section requires preserving other presentations and their routes.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill gates success on a build, route render verification, and settled browser composition checks, with results reported for each.
